content: Amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium, marketed under the brand name AUGMENTIN, is an oral antibacterial combination that consists of two active components: amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium. Clavulanate potassium is the potassium salt of clavulanic acid, which functions as a beta-lactamase inhibitor. Amoxicillin is a semisynthetic derivative of ampicillin, originating from the core penicillin structure known as 6-aminopenicillanic acid. Chemically, amoxicillin is identified as (2S, 5R, 6R)-6-[3,3-dimethyl-7-oxo-4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptane-2-carboxylic acid] trihydrate. Clavulanic acid, on the other hand, is produced through the fermentation of the microorganism Streptomyces clavuligerus. Structurally, it is a beta-lactam compound related to penicillins. Its primary function is to inhibit certain beta-lactamase enzymes by binding to their active sites, thereby preventing the enzymatic degradation of beta-lactam antibiotics.
